subject: Mexico City edge onramp — LatAm dedicated pool feasibility
messages:
From: Ignacio Martinez <ignacio.martinez@novumai.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: maria.lopez@tecnodata.mx
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 13:05:00 -0500
Subject: Exploring a Mexico City onramp — initial ask

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NovumAI is moving forward quickly on a new consumer-facing product for the Mexican market and latency to MX City is a blocker for us. We explored your hosted endpoint but need predictable throughput and data residency for regulatory reasons.

High-level ask: can Redwood provision a small dedicated GPU pool in Mexico City (or colocated in the same metro) to meet a 50ms p99 target for short-form text generation workloads? Initial traffic estimate: 6M tokens/day (burst to 12M), mostly 2–4 token responses, heavy parallelism from mobile clients.

Constraints:
- Compliance: data must not leave MX region for storage/retention >30 days without explicit consent.
- Procurement: NovumAI legal needs a SOW and ballpark cost to start their procurement cycle.
- Timeline: target pilot in Q3 (preferably Aug).

Can you share feasibility, a short capacity estimate, and any gotchas (power/housing/latency expectations)? Maria at TecnoData (cc'd) is our local infra partner — she can assist with datacenter contacts.

Thanks,
Ignacio
Head of Product, NovumAI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Exploring a Mexico City onramp — initial ask

Team,

Attached are three artifacts: a conservative capacity estimate (mexico_city_capacity_estimate.csv), updated rack/cable layout (rack_layout_v2.pdf) and a quick LatAm cost model (latam-cost-model.xlsx). High-level summary below.

Pilot scenario (recommended for Aug):
- Target p99 latency: 50ms for 2–4 token responses; p50 ~10–12ms
- Workload: 6M tokens/day sustained, bursts to 12M/day, request size small but high qps
- Suggested local pool: 4 x A100G (40GB) equivalent pods with continuous batching + small KV cache host. Expected sustained throughput: ~1.0–1.4M tokens/day per GPU depending on batching.
- Autoscale headroom: plan for +2 GPUs for bursts (burst to 6 GPUs).
- Rack footprint: 1 full rack if colocation allows 1U GPUs; depends on vendor. See rack_layout_v2.pdf for example.

Production ramp (3–6 months):
- Increase to 8–12 GPUs regionally (either local MX pool or split across MX + Texas failover) to meet redundancy and SLA.
- Consider fractional resourcing options if colocation cannot supply full A100G units quickly; we can use a hybrid plan with routed capacity from US while MX boots.

Key risks / gotchas:
- Lead time for turnkey A100G provisioning in MX is vendor-dependent; expect 6–10 week hardware procurement + rack build.
- Power density and cooling in some MX City colos may require derated performance or smaller instance counts per rack.
- Data residency: we can implement local KV + retention controls but audit trails must be validated with TecnoData.
- Cost: pilot expected OPEX of ~$36k–$48k/month (local) versus ~$18k–$26k/month routing to nearby US colo (lower latency but cross-border data considerations). See latam-cost-model.xlsx for assumptions.

Recommendation: start pilot with 4 local GPUs + 2 reserved burst GPUs in Texas for immediate coverage. Laura — can you produce the 30-day SOW + pilot pricing so Ignacio can circulate to procurement? Ignacio/Maria — what is your preferred datacenter contact and do you have a target colo partner?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
